'''Engin Arık''' (October 14, 1948 – November 30, 2007) was a Turkish [[particle physicist]] and professor at [[Boğaziçi University]].<ref name="CNN2">[http://edition.cnn.com/2007/WORLD/europe/11/30/turkey.jet/index.html Physics expert, baby among plane dead] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071201120345/http://edition.cnn.com/2007/WORLD/europe/11/30/turkey.jet/index.html |date=2007-12-01 }}, [[CNN]], November 30, 2007.  Retrieved November 30, 2007.</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite journal|last1=Gülmez|first1=Erhan|date=March 2008|title=Faces and places: Engin Arik 1948–2007|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1734190|journal=CERN Courier|volume=48|issue=2|page=36}}</ref> She led the Turkish participation in a number of experiments at [[CERN]]. Arık was a prominent supporter of Turkey's membership to CERN and the founding of a national particle accelerator center as a means to utilize [[thorium]] as an [[Energy development|energy source]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web|date=2010-04-07|title=Hürriyet|url=http://webarsiv.hurriyet.com.tr/2002/07/27/158213.asp|access-date=2021-08-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100407220912/http://webarsiv.hurriyet.com.tr/2002/07/27/158213.asp|archive-date=2010-04-07}}</ref> She has also represented Turkey at the [[Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty Organization|Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty Organization]] for a number of years.<ref name=":0" /> She died in the [[Atlasjet Flight 4203]] crash on November 30, 2007.

== Education ==
Arık graduated from [[Istanbul University]] in 1969 with a [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] in physics and mathematics.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|date=2007-12-05|title=PetroGas|url=http://www.petrogas.com.tr/modules.php?name=Dergi&file=article&sid=20|access-date=2021-08-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071205024606/http://www.petrogas.com.tr/modules.php?name=Dergi&file=article&sid=20|archive-date=2007-12-05}}</ref> As a graduate student, Arik attended [[University of Pittsburgh]] where she earned a master's degree in 1971 and a PhD in 1976 in experimental high energy physics, where she worked on the E583 experiment at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]].<ref name=":3" /> Arık's thesis was titled "Inclusive lambda production in sigma minus - proton collisions at 23 GeV/c."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Publication List|url=http://ocean.phys.boun.edu.tr/~engin/web/publication.html|access-date=2021-08-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071202103321/http://ocean.phys.boun.edu.tr/~engin/web/publication.html|archive-date=2007-12-02}}</ref> Following her PhD, Arık went to [[University of London]], [[Westfield College]] for postdoctoral work. Here she worked in high energy physics research being carried out at the [[Rutherford Appleton Laboratory|Rutherford Laboratory]] and later at the [[CERN]] Laboratory.<ref name=":3" /> While working as a postdoctoral researcher, she contributed to the "measurement of observables in <math>\Pi^+p\rightarrow\Kappa^+\Sigma^+</math>."<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
In 1979, Arık returned to Turkey and joined the Department of Physics at [[Boğaziçi University]], first as a lecturer, then in 1981 as an associate professor.<ref name=":2">[http://www.petrogas.com.tr/modules.php?name=Dergi&file=article&sid=20 Petrogas "Who is Prof. Engin Arık"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071205024606/http://www.petrogas.com.tr/modules.php?name=Dergi&file=article&sid=20|date=2007-12-05}} {{in lang|tr}}</ref> In 1983, Arık briefly left her position at the university to work in industry with [[Control Data Corporation]].<ref name=":0" /> Arık would return to [[Boğaziçi University]] in 1985 and in 1988, she received a full professorship.<ref name=":2" />

While teaching at [[Boğaziçi University]], Arık performed research in the field of [[high energy physics]].<ref name=":0" /> Her work faced limitations due to a scarcity of resources in Turkey available for this area of research.<ref name=":0" /> In the early 1990s she joined experiments at CERN as a collaborator.<ref name=":0" /> Experiments she was a part of include: CHARM II, CHORUS, Spin Muon Collaboration (SMC), [[ATLAS experiment|ATLAS]], and [[CERN Axion Solar Telescope]] (CAST).<ref name=":0" /> During her career Arık supported a movement for Turkey to become a full member of CERN as opposed to an associate member.<ref name=":0" /> A supporter of women in science, she was amongst the founders of the ATLAS Women's Network.<ref>{{cite journal | title = Pioneer and Mentor: A tribute to Engin Arik and her support for Women in Physics | last = Gagnon | first = Pauline | journal = Balkan Physics Letters | year = 2009 | volume = 16 | number = 1 | pages = 46–54}}</ref>

From 1997 to 2000 Arık was appointed to represent Turkey at the [[Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty Organization|Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty Organization]], which was held at the headquarters of the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] (IAEA) in [[Vienna|Vienna, Austria]].<ref name=":3" /> During this time, Arık commuted between Geneva, Istanbul and Vienna.<ref name=":0" /> Arık spoke often about the use of [[thorium]] as an energy source in a new generation of [[Nuclear power plant|Nuclear Power Plants]], calling it "the most strategic material of the 21st century."<ref name=":4" />

Throughout her career, Arık published more than 100 studies in the fields of experimental high energy physics (HEP), detectors, applications of nuclear physics, and mathematical physics.<ref name=":3" /> She was the vice president of the Turkish Physical Society between 2001 and 2003.<ref>{{cite web | language = tr | url = http://tfd.com.tr/Sayfalar/10/Tarihce-.html | title = Tarihçe | trans-title = History | publisher = Turkish Physical Society | access-date = 25 September 2023}}</ref> After she died she was described as a "bannerbearer" for HEP in her country,<ref>{{cite journal | first = Saleh | last = Sultansoy | journal = Balkan Physics Letters | year = 2009 | volume = 17 | pages = 353–358 | arxiv=0905.2874 | title = The Naturalness of the Fourth SM Family}}</ref> and "one of the engin(es)" for the HEP community.<ref name=":0" />

== Death and legacy ==
[[File:EnginArikStreetSign.jpg|thumb|Street Sign named after Engin Arik]]
Arık died in the [[Atlasjet Flight 4203]] crash on November 30, 2007.<ref name="CNN2" /><ref name=":0" /> She was traveling with two students and three colleagues to [[Isparta|Isparta, Turkey]] for the fourth workshop on a potential Turkish particle accelerator design.<ref name=":0" />

After she died a fellowship at CERN was established in her memory.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=ATLAS e-News {{!}} Features|url=https://atlas-service-enews.web.cern.ch/2007-8/features_07-8/features_engin.php|access-date=2021-08-22|website=atlas-service-enews.web.cern.ch}}</ref> Until 2015, the fellowship supported a total of 45 Turkish students so that they could attend CERN's Summer Student Program.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{cite web | title = Geçmiş Yıllarda Engin Arık Bursunu Alan Öğrenciler | access-date = 27 September 2023 | url = https://enginarikfellowship.web.cern.ch/EnginArikBursu/2008-2015.html | trans-title = Students awarded the Engin Arık Fellowship in the past years}}</ref> Funding for the fellowship was provided by institutes, individuals, and private businesses.<ref name=":1" />

An international conference was held at [[Boğaziçi University]] in İstanbul on October 27–31, 2008 in memory of Arık and her colleagues.<ref>{{Cite web|title=International Conference on Particle Physics "In Memoriam" Engin Arık and Her Colleagues|url=https://indico.cern.ch/event/44405/|access-date=2021-08-22|website=Indico}}</ref> Another iteration was held three years later, organized jointly by the [[Doğuş University|Doğuş]] and Boğaziçi Universities, with support from CERN and the [[Turkish Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite journal | title = 2nd International Conference on Particle Physics in memoriam Engin Arık and her Colleagues | doi = 10.1088/1742-6596/347/1/011001 | first1 = Serkant | last1 = Çetin | display-authors = etal | journal = Journal of Physics: Conference Series | year = 2012 | volume = 347 | number = 11001| article-number = 011001 | doi-access = free }}</ref> In 2013, her name was given to the main conference room at the accelerator institute building she helped found. The building is now part of TARLA, the Turkish Accelerator Radiation Laboratory.<ref>{{cite web | title = Enstitü ve Hızlandırıcı Tesisi Hizmet Binalarının Açılışının 2. Yıldönümü Etkinliği | date = 9 May 2013 | language = tr | access-date = 25 September 2023 | url = http://hte.ankara.edu.tr/2014/10/10/enstitu-ve-hizlandirici-tesisi-hizmet-binalarinin-acilisinin-2-yildonumu-etkinligi-9-mayis-2013-2/}}</ref>

A street has been named after Arık in the İlkyerleşim neighborhood of the [[Yenimahalle]] district in [[Ankara]], Turkey.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.google.com/maps/place/%C4%B0lkyerle%C5%9Fim,+Prof.+Dr.+Engin+Ar%C4%B1k+Sk.,+06370+Yenimahalle%2FAnkara/@39.9717683,32.7295823,17z | title = Prof. Dr. Engin Arık Sk. | publisher = Google Maps | access-date = 25 September 2023}}</ref> A monument at the [[Süleyman Demirel University]] commemorating the six scientists who died at the plane crash has a bust of Arık specifically.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://haber.sdu.edu.tr/haber/3345/prof-dr-engin-arik-ve-bilim-sehitleri-anildi | title = Prof. Dr. Engin Arık ve Bilim Şehitleri Anıldı | language = tr | date = 2 December 2019 | access-date = 25 September 2023 | publisher = [[Süleyman Demirel University]]}}</ref>

== Assassination allegations ==
There are various assassination allegations about Engin Arık's death. After the plane crash, some groups claimed that it was an assassination and that the accident was preplanned.<ref>{{cite news | title = Toryum ve uçak kazası: Bir suikast mı? | language = tr | url = https://www.cumhuriyet.com.tr/yazi-dizileri/toryum-ve-ucak-kazasi-bir-suikast-mi-1984158 | author = Özdemir İnce | date = 23 September 2022 | access-date = 25 September 2023 | publisher = Cumhuriyet}}</ref> An investigation has been opened on this issue and is still ongoing.
